purpose: Everything the Conifer SDK reads. If the SDK consumes it, it is named here. The logic in src/ reads this card's fields and nothing else.

apiKey.note: The entitlement credential. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on the OpenAI door and `x-api-key` on the Anthropic door. Never logged, never placed in a URL.

baseUrl.note: Gateway origin WITHOUT the /v1 suffix. The OpenAI door is `${baseUrl}/v1`; the Anthropic Messages door is `${baseUrl}/v1/messages`.

fetch.note: Injected so tests and edge runtimes supply their own transport. The SDK opens no socket of its own.

timeoutMs.note: Client-side abort. Chosen to match the gateway's own 300s edge silent-cut (contracts/gateway-contract.json timeouts_secs.edge_silent_cut) so the client never gives up on a turn the gateway is still serving.

maxRetries.note: Retries apply ONLY to transport faults and to 429/502/503/504. A 4xx the gateway authored (400/401/402/404/409/422) is never retried: the same bytes are refused again. Every retry of a POST carries the SAME idempotency key, so a retried turn cannot double-bill.

defaultHeaders.note: Merged under the SDK's own headers. Cannot overwrite the credential.

request_options.note: Per-call knobs. Each maps to a REAL gateway input; nothing here is invented client-side except `fallbackModels`, which is explicitly a client-side chain (see portability.card.json).

model.note: Accepts `vendor/model` spellings; the gateway resolves the last segment when the full id is absent.

stream.note: SSE. `stream_options.include_usage` is set for you when `stream: true`, so the final usage chunk always arrives.

maxCostNanoUsd.note: HARD ceiling on the caller-total worst case. Over-ceiling requests are REFUSED (402/`cost_ceiling_exceeded`) before any upstream call.

deadlineSeconds.note: ADVISORY. Only widens how a turn may be served (flex tier). Never changes auth, model, or price.

defer.note: Submits the turn as a DEFERRED JOB. Answered with 202 and a JOB ENVELOPE (job_id/status/deadline_utc/poll_url) — NOT a completion, which is why `chat()` REFUSES this flag and `defer()` exists to return the job. The gateway requires a completion window of at least 86400s and refuses a narrower one rather than serving it synchronously, so `defer()` defaults to that floor. The job is accepted AND DEBITED at submission.

venue.note: HARD constraint. This gateway is the cloud venue; `local` is refused, never silently satisfied.

idempotencyKey.note: Bound to the request body by the gateway. Reusing a key with a different body is refused, not served the prior result.

promptCache.note: Only `"off"` is meaningful: it opts this one request out of prompt-cache annotation, so no +25% cache-write class is charged. The header can never turn caching ON.

requestId.note: YOUR id for this turn, and the one that comes back in the receipt. The gateway derives its request id from the FIRST of `idempotency-key` then `x-request-id` (its own `request_id()`, confirmed live 2026-08-27) — and the SDK always sends an idempotency key, so `x-request-id` alone was NEVER reached and this field was inert. On this gateway the two are ONE identity, so an explicit requestId now feeds the idempotency key as well. Consequence, stated because it is real: the key is bound to the request BODY, so reusing one requestId across two different bodies is a 409 `request_in_progress`, not two turns. Pass idempotencyKey explicitly to control the two separately.

client.note: Your app's name, for your own usage attribution.

serverFallbackModels.note: The GATEWAY-side fallback chain (gateway PR typhoon#356): models it tries, in order, when the requested model fails UPSTREAM — 5xx, 429, timeout/transport, an unreadable body, or a proven upstream 4xx shape refusal (the DeepSeek 422 class) when a DIFFERENT model is still ahead. ONE request: the gateway holds money once for the whole chain, settles ONCE against whichever member served, and refunds in full if none did. Never triggers on the gateway's OWN refusals (401/402/400/404 — those precede any upstream call), and never after a byte of a stream reached the client. Every member is admitted like a primary before any spend; an unknown/unserved id is a 400 NAMING it, never a silent skip. Duplicates and the requested model itself are DROPPED (harmless, not wrong) — the SDK mirrors that rather than being stricter than the wire, and sends no header at all when nothing survives. At most 3 members after de-duplication. Credits lane only; refused on a BYOK primary and with defer. Disclosed on the receipt: effectiveModel names the member that served and reason reads `provider_failover`.

fallbackModels.note: The CLIENT-side chain, kept for callers who want the retry in their own process. NOTE: `serverFallbackModels` above is now the better answer for almost every case — it is one request, one bill, and it can act on failures the client never sees. The SDK therefore walks the chain ITSELF, one full request per member, and reports which member served in the result's `fallbackIndex`. Honest, not free: each attempt is its own billed turn only if it reached upstream, and only retryable failures advance the chain.

embeddings_request.note: `POST /v1/embeddings`, reached as `conifer.embeddings.create(...)` (TS) / `client.embed(...)` (Python). Embeddings bill on INPUT ONLY — there is no completion, so the catalog carries a zero output rate for every embedding seat. That is why this door has no maxTokens, no sampling knobs and no stream: none of them mean anything here, and offering them would imply a control the wire does not have.

model.note: Must DECLARE `caps: ["embeddings"]`. A chat model is a 400 naming the chat door, not an opaque upstream 404 on your money.

input.note: A string, or an array of strings; a batch returns one vector per member, index ascending. Token-id arrays are REFUSED client-side, before any spend: the gateway cannot size a hold from token ids it did not tokenize, and serving an unpriced turn is the one thing the money path must never do.

dimensions.note: Matryoshka shortening. Forwarded verbatim; the upstream validates it.

encodingFormat.note: DEFAULTS TO `base64`, which the SDK then decodes for you into plain numbers. A JSON float array spends ~20 bytes per dimension against base64 float32's 5.33, so this is ~3x less network on the one payload that is actually large. Safe to do silently ONLY because it is exactly lossless: verified live 2026-08-27, text-embedding-3-small returned identical values both ways, max abs difference 0.0. Pass `"float"` for JSON floats on the wire; `raw` always holds the provider's own body.

user.note: Opaque end-user id, forwarded verbatim for the provider's own abuse tooling.

idempotencyKey.note: Same rule as chat: every POST carries one, so a transport retry cannot bill twice.

requestId.note: YOUR id for this turn, and the one that comes back in the receipt. The gateway derives its request id from the FIRST of `idempotency-key` then `x-request-id` (its own `request_id()`, confirmed live 2026-08-27) — and the SDK always sends an idempotency key, so `x-request-id` alone was NEVER reached and this field was inert. On this gateway the two are ONE identity, so an explicit requestId now feeds the idempotency key as well. Consequence, stated because it is real: the key is bound to the request BODY, so reusing one requestId across two different bodies is a 409 `request_in_progress`, not two turns. Pass idempotencyKey explicitly to control the two separately.

environment.CONIFER_BASE_URL: override the gateway origin (staging, a local gateway)
environment.OPENAI_BASE_URL: read ONLY as a fallback when CONIFER_BASE_URL is unset and it already points at a Conifer host, so a drop-in env survives

deferred_jobs.note: The read/cancel plane for deferred work: `conifer.jobs.*` (TS) / `job_status`/`job_result`/`job_cancel`/`jobs_wait` (Python). The accept arm rides POST /v1/chat/completions.
deferred_jobs.GET /v1/deferred/{id}: status only — no content, no cost. TENANCY: a foreign job id and a nonexistent one are the SAME 404, so a 404 means 'not yours or not real', never 'not yet'.
deferred_jobs.GET /v1/deferred/{id}/result: the completion with its settled receipt. 409 while running, AND for every terminal state with no result (cancelled/failed/expired — all refunded for unfinished work). Fetching moves the job to `fetched` and starts the retention grace, after which the body is deleted.
deferred_jobs.POST /v1/deferred/{id}/cancel: refunded per the gateway's cancel rules.
deferred_jobs.states: queued → submitted → ended → fetched, plus expired/cancelled/failed. TERMINAL = fetched/expired/cancelled/failed. `ended` is deliberately NOT terminal: it is where the result becomes fetchable, and treating it as an end would skip collecting it.
deferred_jobs.wait(): polls with exponential backoff, STOPS on a terminal state (a loop keyed only on 'is it ended' spins forever on a cancelled job), and on timeout raises WITHOUT cancelling — killing work the caller paid for on a client-side clock is not the SDK's decision.
